files.purpose: The Codex provider session driver: a @MainActor final class CodexSession conforming to ProviderSession that spawns `codex app-server` over stdio JSON-RPC and translates the whole Codex app-server protocol (thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, thread/rollback, thread/archive, thread/compact/start, turn/start, turn/interrupt, thread/turns/list, skills/list, model/list, account/rateLimits/read, account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume) into Droppy's ProviderEvent stream, including Hydra multi-head (spawned sub-agent) thread tracking, token ledger accounting, approval/permission/question requests, and runtime-mode sandbox policy mapping.

side_effects: Launches the `codex` executable as a child process with the single argument "app-server" via StdioProcess, in configuration.workingDirectory with configuration.environment

JSON-RPC requests over that process's stdio: initialize, thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, thread/rollback, thread/archive, thread/turns/list, thread/compact/start, turn/start, turn/interrupt, skills/list, model/list, account/rateLimits/read, account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume
JSON-RPC notification `initialized` sent after initialize succeeds

JSON-RPC responses sent back for item/commandExecution/requestApproval, item/fileChange/requestApproval, item/permissions/requestApproval, item/tool/requestUserInput and mcpServer/elicitation/request; error -32601 for any other request method
Records token spend globally through TokenLedger.shared.record(spend:) for both lead and head threads
Watchdog Tasks that close the connection: 20 seconds in connect(), 20 seconds in listCommands, 30 seconds in rollback(from:)
OSLog notices (subsystem iordv.droppycode, category codex) when a head is taken in by agent nickname or registered from a subAgentActivity note
Archives Codex threads on the server (thread/archive) during the rollback fork path, mutating the user's Codex conversation store
Generates a fresh lowercased UUID as idempotencyKey per reset-credit consume call
Reads MCP server configuration through MCPProviderConfig.codexOverrides() (file-backed; no file means none)
Passes local image file paths to the model as {"type":"localImage","path":...} content parts
Connects with FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory as the working directory for listModels, readPlanLimits and consumeResetCredit
platform_assumptions: @MainActor isolation for the whole class: every notification handler and event callback runs on the main thread (AppKit/SwiftUI main-actor model)
Swift Concurrency: async/await, Task, Task.sleep(for: .seconds(...)), Task.isCancelled, detached watchdog tasks
OSLog's Logger with privacy: .public string interpolation (Apple unified logging)
Foundation URL and FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory for the throwaway working directory of catalog/plan-limit calls
Unix-style stdio child-process JSON-RPC via StdioProcess; `codex` must be a POSIX executable resolvable at configuration.executable
Swift 5.9+ switch-expression syntax used for the sink, status, verb and policySettings mappings
Depends on the Codex CLI subcommand `app-server` existing and speaking this JSON-RPC dialect
persisted_fields: Nothing is persisted by this file to disk or UserDefaults; all state is in-memory per session

ui_elements: Warning notice: "Codex refused the MCP server configuration, so this session runs without MCP servers. Check MCP in Settings."
Info notice on thread/compacted: "Context compacted."
Retry warning notice: the error message, a space, then "Retrying."
MCP elicitation decline notice: "<serverName> asked for input, which Droppy Code cannot show yet." with serverName falling back to "An MCP server"

Approval option titles: accept -> "Approve" (.approve), acceptForSession -> "Approve for session" (.approveAlways), decline -> "Decline" (.decline), cancel -> "Stop turn" (.cancel), amend -> "Always allow" (.approveAlways, id "amend")
Permissions approval options: id "turn" title "Allow once" role .approve; id "session" title "Allow for session" role .approveAlways; id "decline" title "Decline" role .decline
File-change approval title: "Apply file changes"; detail is params.grantRoot
Permission description parts: "Write to " + paths joined by ", "; "Read " + paths joined by ", "; "Network access"; parts joined with " \u00b7 "; fallback "Additional permissions"

Collab tool verbs: spawnAgent -> "Send out a head"; sendInput/sendMessage/followupTask -> "Brief a head"; wait -> "Wait for heads"; closeAgent/interruptAgent -> "Recall a head"; resumeAgent -> "Resume a head"; listAgents -> "List heads"; default -> "Agent"

Head descriptions: preview single-lined at limit 80, else nickname and role joined " \u00b7 ", else "Subagent"; spawn brief single-lined at limit 80 else "Head"; subAgentActivity nickname is the last "/" component of agentPath with "_" replaced by " ", else "Head"
Collab tool call brief uses TextCleanup.singleLine(prompt, limit: 90)
Multi-file edit title: "Edit \(paths.count) files"
MCP tool title format "<server> \u00b7 <tool>" with fallbacks "MCP" and "tool"
Fallback tool titles: "Command", "Tool", "Web search", "Image", "Generate image", "Review"

Thrown user-visible errors: "Codex could not resume the original conversation.", "Codex did not start a thread.", "Codex did not return its conversation history.", "Codex returned a turn without an ID.", "Codex could not page its conversation history.", "Codex could not find the selected turn. The conversation was kept.", "Codex did not confirm the requested conversation rollback.", "Codex did not create a conversation at the revert point.", "Codex did not confirm the reverted conversation history."

Plan-limit problem strings: "Codex's stored login has expired. Run `codex login` in a terminal, then check again.", "Codex could not be asked for its usage.", "Codex reported no usage windows for this account."
Default error message: "Codex reported an error."
Unsupported-method JSON-RPC error: code -32601, message "Droppy Code does not support <method>."
Plan window title is PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes:) suffixed with " \u00b7 <limitName>" when there is more than one snapshot; window id is "<limitId or 'codex'>-<primary|secondary>"
initialize clientInfo shown to the server: name "droppy-code", title "Droppy Code", version AppInfo.version
feature_notes: start(): throws ProviderError.notInstalled(configuration.provider) when configuration.executable is nil; on resume it sends thread/resume with threadId plus excludeTurns=true and requires the returned thread.id to equal the requested id; otherwise thread/start. activeModel is taken from result["model"]. A defer closes and nils the connection when `started` never became true.

requestThread MCP retry: when the RPCError message contains "failed to load configuration" or "invalid transport" AND params.config.mcp_servers exists, it strips mcp_servers (and drops config entirely if that leaves it empty), retries the same method, and emits the MCP warning notice.

send(): content is input.command?.codexInput(for: input.text) or [["type":"text","text": text]]; each image where isImage appends {"type":"localImage","path": path}. It always sets "summary": "auto". An empty effort string is dropped. serviceTierForTurn comes from input.serviceTier. collaborationMode is sent only when a model resolves (input.model ?? activeModel), with mode "plan" for .plan interaction mode else "default", and settings {model, reasoning_effort (optional), developer_instructions: null}. The returned turn.id is stored in turnID.
interrupt() sends turn/interrupt with threadId and turnId, ignoring failures; compact() sends thread/compact/start with just threadId.

rollback(from:): a 30-second watchdog closes the connection. It pages thread/turns/list with limit 100, sortDirection "desc", itemsView "notLoaded", counting turns until targetID is found, then taking the next turn as previousID. It throws if nextCursor repeats the current cursor. Then thread/rollback with numTurns = count; the result must keep the same thread id, must no longer contain targetID, and its last remaining turn id must equal previousID. It clears turnID and returns threadID.
Rollback fallback: an RPCError containing "paginated threads do not support thread/rollback" routes to forkHistory.

forkHistory: with no previousID it archives the original thread, clears threadID and turnID, and returns nil. Otherwise it forks using threadParameters plus threadId, lastTurnId=previousID, excludeTurns=true; requires the new id to differ from the original; confirms via a 1-turn desc listing that the newest turn is previousID and not targetID; archives the original. On any failure it archives the NEW thread and rethrows. On success threadID becomes the new id, turnID is cleared, activeModel is refreshed.
threadParameters always sends cwd, approvalPolicy, sandbox, approvalsReviewer; model only when configuration.model is set.

Hydra native (hydra.runsNatively): merges HydraPrompts.codexConfig(hydra) into config with hydra's values winning on collision, and sets developerInstructions to HydraPrompts.policy(for: .codex, hydra).

Hydra non-native (heads on another provider, Droppy-run): sets config.features.multi_agent = false to switch off Codex's own agents whatever the user's config enables, and developerInstructions to HydraPrompts.fallbackPolicy(hydra). The in-source comment records that words alone were not enough: a lead still reached for spawn_agent, ran its heads on itself, and the pair's model never saw them.

Anti-slop guidance rides along on every thread, Hydra or not: any existing developerInstructions and AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled: configuration.antiSlopEnabled) are joined with "\n\n" (nils compacted out), so the off notice still goes out and a resumed thread cannot keep earlier guidance alive.
MCPProviderConfig.codexOverrides() is merged into config["mcp_servers"] on top of whatever config already exists, never replacing it.

resolveApproval: .decision responds {"decision": payloads[optionID] ?? "cancel"}; .permissions responds {"permissions": requested, "scope": optionID} for optionID "turn" or "session" and {"permissions": {}, "scope": "turn"} otherwise; .question responds {"answers": {}}. It always emits .requestResolved(id:).
answerQuestion builds {"answers": {questionID: {"answers": [values]}}} and emits .requestResolved(id:).
stop() sets isStopping then closes the connection; handleClose resolves every pending request first and, unless stopping, emits .exited(error: TextCleanup.lastLines(tail)).
stopAgent(id) returns false unless the id is a known head with a live turn; it sends turn/interrupt on the head's own thread id.
listCommands: connects with no handlers, sets a 20-second watchdog, closes on defer, sends skills/list with cwds=[directory.path] and forceReload=true, and maps through SlashCommand.codexSkills.

listModels: connects against FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory, pages model/list at most 10 times following nextCursor, skips any model where hidden == true, requires an id, and falls back name -> id, isDefault -> false.
fastTier: builds "<id> <name>" lowercased and returns the first tier id whose label contains "fast" or "priority".

readPlanLimits: on a request failure it returns PlanLimits(planName: nil, windows: [], problem: plainProblem(error)). Snapshots come from rateLimitsByLimitId sorted by key, else the single non-null rateLimits object. Each snapshot's "primary" and "secondary" windows need a usedPercent double; window ids are "<limitId or 'codex'>-<key>"; resetsAt is treated as epoch seconds. With no windows it returns problem "Codex reported no usage windows for this account." with the parsed plan name.

plainProblem: TextCleanup.singleLine(String(describing: error), limit: 300); text containing "token_expired" or "401" becomes the codex login message; empty text becomes "Codex could not be asked for its usage."
parseResetCredits: requires availableCount or available_count; keeps credits with a non-empty id whose status is nil, "available" or "unknown"; availableCount is clamped with max(0, count).

resetDate accepts a number or numeric string (must be > 0), treating any value above 10_000_000_000 as milliseconds (divided by 1_000), else tries ISO 8601 with fractional seconds and then plain ISO 8601.

consumeResetCredit always sends idempotencyKey = UUID().uuidString.lowercased() and optionally creditId; it throws ResetCreditError.unknownOutcome when result.outcome is missing or not a PlanLimits.ResetOutcome raw value.

connect(): StdioProcess with arguments ["app-server"], JSONRPCConnection(process:, sendsVersion: false), a 20-second watchdog, an initialize request with clientInfo {name: "droppy-code", title: "Droppy Code", version: AppInfo.version} and capabilities {experimentalApi: true}; on failure it closes and rethrows; on success it sends the `initialized` notification.

handleNotification routes by params.threadId: a missing or matching id is the lead; a known head thread becomes .head(id) whose events are wrapped in .agentEvent(agentID:); notifications from any other thread on the same server are dropped entirely.
thread/started is handled before routing, by headStarted.
turn/started stores the turn id on the lead (turnID) or on headTurns[head], and emits .turnStarted(providerTurnID:).

item/agentMessage/delta -> .messageDelta; item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta and item/reasoning/textDelta -> .reasoningDelta; item/commandExecution/outputDelta -> .toolOutput; item/plan/delta -> .planDelta.
item/reasoning/summaryPartAdded emits a literal "\n\n" reasoning delta only when summaryIndex > 0.
turn/plan/updated maps step status "completed" -> .done, "inProgress" -> .active, anything else -> .pending, and emits .todos.
turn/diff/updated emits .diff(diff) when a diff string is present.

Lead token accounting on thread/tokenUsage/updated: emits ContextUsage(usedTokens: last.totalTokens ?? 0, windowTokens: tokenUsage.modelContextWindow). When total.totalTokens > 0 it calls spendTracker.spend(total:before: max(0, total - used)) so a resumed thread starts from total-minus-last rather than zero, and records only positive spend; otherwise it records `used` directly. The comment notes the thread total only ever grows within a session, so its positive deltas are exact spend however often the event fires.

Head token accounting mirrors the lead with a per-head TokenSpendTracker (a head's spend is the account's spend too) and additionally emits .agentProgress(agentID: head, summary: nil, lastTool: nil, tokens: total > 0 ? total : used, toolCalls: nil).
The "error" notification only raises a warning notice when it belongs to the lead and willRetry == true.

turn/completed maps turn.status "interrupted" -> .interrupted, "failed" -> .failed, default -> .completed; a null turn.error is treated as no error. For the lead it clears turnID, and a failed turn whose error matches UsageLimitSignal also emits .usageLimit(resetsAt: UsageLimitSignal.resetTime(in: error)) before .turnCompleted. For a head it clears headTurns[head] and emits .agentFinished(agentID:status:summary: error).
serverRequest/resolved clears a matching pending request by RPCID key and emits .requestResolved.

headStarted: a thread whose parentThreadId equals the lead's threadID is taken as a head. A thread naming another parent is still taken in when it carries agentNickname or agentRole (covering a resumed lead whose id rotated), and that case is logged at notice level with the thread id, the named parent (or "none") and this lead's id.

itemStarted: agentMessage emits a messageDelta of item.text (or ""), reasoning emits an empty reasoningDelta, plan emits a planDelta of item.text. A head's first userMessage becomes .agentStarted with the brief single-lined at 80 characters. hookPrompt, functionCallOutput and contextCompaction are ignored. Anything else that yields a ToolCall emits .toolStarted, and a collabAgentToolCall additionally registers its heads immediately so a completion lost to compaction never leaves them unknown.

itemCompleted: agentMessage -> .messageCompleted; reasoning joins summary[] with "\n\n" and falls back to content[] joined the same way; plan -> .planCompleted(markdown:). userMessage, hookPrompt, functionCallOutput and contextCompaction are ignored. Anything else that yields a ToolCall emits .toolStarted then .toolUpdated, and describeHeads runs on either target because the payload says whose head it is whatever thread the server filed it under.

describeHeads on collabAgentToolCall acts only when item.tool == "spawnAgent"; every receiverThreadIds entry is inserted into headThreads and announced as .agentStarted with toolUseID = item.id. A spawn whose item.model and item.reasoningEffort match exactly one HydraPrompts.nativeRoutableProfiles entry routes the head to that profile name; zero or several matches leave the head unrouted.

describeHeads on subAgentActivity registers an unseen agentThreadId as a head (logged at notice level explaining no thread/started or spawn receiver id preceded it, for older app-servers), then on kind "completed" or "interrupted" clears its turn and emits .agentFinished with the matching status and nil summary.

toolCall for commandExecution: when the set of commandAction types is exactly {"read"} and the first action has a path, it becomes a .read call titled by relative path with the unwrapped command as detail; when the set is non-empty and a subset of {"search", "listFiles"} it becomes .search titled by the command; otherwise .command. The command is always unwrapped via ToolTitles.unwrapShell.
toolCall for fileChange titles a single change by relative path, otherwise "Edit <n> files", kind .edit.
toolCall for mcpToolCall sets detail to the compact arguments string unless that string is literally "null".

toolCall for dynamicToolCall -> .other titled by item.tool; webSearch -> .web titled by item.query; imageView -> .read titled by relative path; imageGeneration -> .other titled by revisedPrompt; enteredReviewMode/exitedReviewMode -> .other titled "Review" with item.review as detail.
toolCall returns nil for subAgentActivity, so those rows draw nothing; the comment explains they only doubled the head's report pill as "Delegated Head finished".

toolUpdate for commandExecution sets output from aggregatedOutput and exitCode from exitCode; for fileChange it builds FileEdits with relative paths and ToolTitles.diffStats additions/deletions; for mcpToolCall it prefers error.message, else joins result.content[].text with "\n"; webSearch, imageView, enteredReviewMode and exitedReviewMode are marked .completed unconditionally.
toolStatus maps "inProgress" -> .running, "failed" and "interrupted" -> .failed, "declined" -> .declined, and otherwise .failed when a non-zero exitCode exists else .completed.
errorMessage takes error.message or error.displayText, and when that raw text itself parses as JSON containing error.message or message, the nested message wins.

decisionOptions defaults availableDecisions to ["accept", "acceptForSession", "decline", "cancel"]; an object decision carrying acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment adds the "amend" option only for command approvals; options are sorted into the order approve, approveAlways, decline, cancel (missing roles sort as index 0).

handleRequest covers item/commandExecution/requestApproval (title is the unwrapped command or "Command", detail is the relative cwd), item/fileChange/requestApproval, item/permissions/requestApproval, item/tool/requestUserInput, and mcpServer/elicitation/request which is auto-declined with {"action":"decline"} plus a warning notice; every other method gets JSON-RPC error -32601.
Question requests always set allowsMultiple: false; allowsOther comes from isOther and isSecret from isSecret (both default false); header and prompt fall back to empty strings; choices need a label.

policySettings mapping by RuntimeMode: .supervised -> approvalPolicy "untrusted", sandbox "read-only", sandboxPolicy {"type":"readOnly"}, reviewer "user"; .autoAcceptEdits -> "on-request", "workspace-write", {"type":"workspaceWrite"}, "user"; .auto -> "on-request", "workspace-write", {"type":"workspaceWrite"}, "auto_review"; .fullAccess -> "never", "danger-full-access", {"type":"dangerFullAccess"}, "user".

threadParameters sends the `sandbox` string form while send() sends the `sandboxPolicy` object form alongside approvalPolicy and approvalsReviewer on every turn, so the runtime mode can change between turns without restarting the thread.
unresolved_questions: The exact shape of HydraPrompts.codexConfig(hydra) (which Codex config keys it sets) is not visible here; only that its keys win over any already in `config` on merge.
MCPProviderConfig.codexOverrides() returns the JSONValue placed at config.mcp_servers, but its structure and the file it reads are defined elsewhere.
TurnInput.command.codexInput(for:) (how a slash command becomes input content parts) is defined outside this file.
JSONValue's .compactString and .displayText formatting rules are not defined here, so the exact MCP arguments detail text and the raw error text cannot be pinned from this file alone.
PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes:) and PlanLimitsReader.codexPlanName(_:) produce the user-visible window and plan names; their literals live in another file.
Whether `sendsVersion: false` on JSONRPCConnection omits the jsonrpc version field or some client-version field is not determinable from this file.
UsageLimitSignal.matches/resetTime matching patterns are not in this file.
PlanLimits.ResetOutcome's raw values are not listed here, only that result.outcome must parse into one.

The file has no compile-time conditionals or feature flags and every branch appears reachable at runtime; the acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment option and the thread/rollback-to-fork fallback are version-dependent on the installed app-server, which this source alone cannot determine.
